summary: Workflow .github/workflows/docs-link-check.yml is correct, well-scoped, and isolated from cargo CI. YAML parses cleanly. Triggers, paths filter, action pin, --offline, and fail:true all match Decision 5 / tech-spec Task 11 spec. No interference with ci.yml (orthogonal paths-ignore vs paths filters keep cargo and docs jobs mutually exclusive on doc-only PRs). Commit scope is exactly the new workflow file plus the task status flip.

findings.summary: Scope clean: commit 124e663 touches only .github/workflows/docs-link-check.yml (29 lines added) and tasks/11.md status. ci.yml is unchanged.

YAML is well-formed (python yaml.safe_load passes). Structure: name, on.push (branches dev/main + paths), on.pull_request (paths), concurrency group, single job lychee-link-check on ubuntu-latest with actions/checkout@v4 and lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2 (--offline --no-progress, fail: true).

ci.yml uses paths-ignore on '*.md', 'docs/**', 'work/**', '.claude/**', 'LICENSE'; docs-link-check.yml uses paths on 'docs/**', '*.md', and the workflow file itself. The two trigger sets are disjoint by design — doc-only PRs run only docs-link-check, code PRs run only cargo CI. Matches Decision 5 rationale.
Both actions pinned by major tag (actions/checkout@v4, lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2). No secrets referenced; --offline avoids any external network calls. No write permissions requested.

args glob 'docs/**/*.md' relies on lychee-action's shell globbing; 'docs/WHITEPAPER.md' is explicitly listed but is also matched by the glob, so it is redundant (no functional harm). README.md at repo root is included explicitly, which is correct because the glob does not cover it. Optional follow-up: drop the redundant 'docs/WHITEPAPER.md' or replace the explicit list with a single args block. Non-blocking.

All AC met: file exists; paths filter present on push and pull_request including the workflow file itself; lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2 with --offline; fail: true; YAML parses; ci.yml unchanged; single commit with conventional 'ci:' scope.
